skill.name: create-new-skills
skill.description: Creates new Agent Skills for Claude Code following best practices and documentation. Use when the user wants to create a new skill, extend Claude's capabilities, or package domain expertise into a reusable skill.
skill.summary: Guides agents through planning, authoring, testing, and sharing Claude Code skills.
skill.author: EGAdams

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, normal Claude Code skill paths, and documentation snippets. One external-command workflow risk remains: the skill presents git commit and push as standard publishing steps without an explicit user approval gate.

remediation.issue: Git publishing is presented as a normal final step.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running git commit or git push, and show the exact files and remote branch first.

remediation.issue: The remove-skill documentation uses rm -rf on a personal skill path.
remediation.suggestion: Add a path verification step or suggest moving the skill directory to a backup location before permanent deletion.

remediation.issue: Skill names are used in shell path examples.
remediation.suggestion: State that generated skill names must be sanitized to lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens before any shell command is run.

semantic_findings.title: Version Control Publication Without Approval Gate
semantic_findings.description: The skill workflow tells the agent to commit and push generated skill files as a normal final step. This can publish unreviewed skill instructions to a shared repository if the user has not explicitly approved the remote update.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both cited sections include git commit and git push steps for sharing skills. The issue is workflow intent and missing consent, not command syntax alone.

content.value_statement: Reusable agent skills are hard to structure and test consistently. This skill guides Claude or Codex through planning, authoring, testing, and sharing Claude Code skills.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of SKILL.md files with required YAML frontmatter.
Helps choose project or personal skill directory locations.
Explains how to organize instructions, examples, scripts, templates, and references.
Provides testing steps for file structure, frontmatter, and trigger behavior.
Includes examples for code review, CSV analysis, documentation, and skill extension.
Describes team sharing through project skills and version control.
limitations: It does not include automation scripts that generate a complete skill automatically.
It focuses on Claude Code skill structure, not every marketplace packaging format.
The user must define the skill scope, triggers, examples, and resource content.
Version control publishing steps should be reviewed before execution.

use_cases.title: Create a Project Skill
use_cases.description: Define a team skill, build the SKILL.md structure, add examples, and test discovery in Claude Code.

use_cases.title: Package Domain Workflows
use_cases.description: Turn repeated operating procedures into reusable instructions with supporting files and templates.

use_cases.title: Extend an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Add a new capability, supporting reference file, or example to an existing skill while preserving its scope.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner skill creation from a simple idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code skill for reviewing Python files. Ask any required scope questions, then draft the skill structure and testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate conversion of a repeated process into a skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this repeated workflow into a reusable skill: [paste workflow]. Define triggers, required files, examples, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-File Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced skill with references, templates, and optional scripts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-file Claude Code skill for [domain]. Include the file layout, progressive disclosure plan, script guidance, and test checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Extend and Audit a Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced update of an existing skill with safety review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this existing skill and add [capability]. Keep the scope focused, update examples, identify risks, and list tests before publishing.

output_examples.input: Create a skill that reviews Python code for security and performance.
output: A short scope questionnaire for review criteria and target frameworks.
A proposed skill directory name and frontmatter description.
A workflow covering file reading, issue review, line references, and final reporting.
Three test prompts to confirm the skill triggers correctly.

output_examples.input: Build a skill for analyzing CSV data with charts and a report.
output: A multi-file plan with instructions, scripts, and a report template.
Guidance for when the agent should run scripts versus read reference files.
Examples for summary statistics, visualization, and custom reporting.

output_examples.input: Add spell correction to our transcription skill.
output: A focused extension plan for the existing workflow.
A supporting correction reference file and updated examples.
A testing checklist for common transcription errors.

best_practices: Start by defining the skill trigger, user task, and expected output.
Keep the main instructions focused and move specialized details into linked files.
Test the skill with realistic prompts before sharing it with a team.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated workflows into one broad skill.
Do not publish generated skills without reviewing commands and file changes.
Do not rely on vague descriptions that make skill triggering unpredictable.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code Agent Skills with frontmatter, instructions, examples, optional resources, and test steps.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It is written for Claude Code skills, but Codex can follow the authoring workflow and documentation guidance.

faq.question: Does it create files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow and examples. The agent still needs to create or edit files in the user workspace.

faq.question: Does it support multi-file skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to add supporting instructions, scripts, templates, examples, and reference documents.

faq.question: How should team sharing be handled?
faq.answer: Use project skills or plugins, then review changes before committing or pushing them to a shared repository.

faq.question: What should be tested before using a new skill?
faq.answer: Check the file structure, validate YAML frontmatter, and run realistic prompts that should trigger the skill.
